You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. # - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket visibly closed more than in the input image, with its front panels brought together at least in part?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows the jacket's front panels brought together along some portion of the closure compared with the input. Fail if the jacket is visibly unchanged or more open. Unknown if the closure cannot be assessed from the image or comparison evidence is insufficient.
node.binding: Assess only the woman's jacket identified in the input image; judge visible change to its front closure, not unrelated edits.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket’s front is visibly more open in the edited image, with a panel hanging away from her body, rather than brought together compared with the source.

fulfillment: The node’s target and completion criterion are clear, and the traces are valid, queried, and high-confidence; this is not a transport or schema failure. The images do show the edited jacket hanging open, while the source also appears open, so the checks’ claim that it became *more* open is not clearly established by this comparison. Keep the full-closure requirement, but make the progress decision depend on an explicit source-versus-edit comparison: distinguish unchanged openness from a visible move toward closure, and count only evidenced progress. The reference label says the aggregate should be yes, but does not identify which visual criterion or check is wrong; investigate the apparent conflict rather than overriding the image evidence or forcing yes. If the source/edit comparison is genuinely ambiguous, preserve unknown rather than treating uncertainty as failure.
s2: The binding already identifies the correct jacket and makes full closure the endpoint; do not weaken that requirement or infer success from the reference label. The edited image shows the woman turned sideways with the jacket front obscured/partly hidden by the hanging panel, so the trace’s confident claim that an opening remains is not securely supported by visible closure evidence. Refine the node’s evidence rule to distinguish a clearly visible open closure from a closure that is merely occluded, using unknown when the front cannot be assessed. Keep partial closure distinct from full closure, and avoid relying on the parent’s unsupported claim that the jacket became more open; assess source-to-edit progress only where the same closure is comparably visible. The execution is valid and queried, so this is a visual-evidence/confidence issue, not transport or schema failure.

response.content: {"text":"The binding targets the right garment, but the criterion should explicitly separate the requested endpoint (fully closed) from the rubric’s progress judgment (any visible movement toward closure). Compare the same front-closure area in source and edit: count partial progress only when panels are visibly brought together more than before; unchanged openness is no progress, and a clearly more-open jacket is not progress. In these images the source front is also difficult to assess, while the edited woman is turned sideways and the hanging panel obscures the closure. The trace’s confident claim of increased openness is therefore not securely grounded; use unknown when orientation or occlusion prevents a reliable comparison, rather than treating hidden closure as visibly open or as progress. The valid, queried execution indicates a visual-evidence issue, not transport/schema failure. Treat the reference label as an aggregate constraint to investigate, not atomic proof or a reason to force yes."}
